newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares end sharply down after record high.
newsitem.headline: French shares end sharply down after record high.

text.p: French shares closed sharply lower on Thursday on profit-taking triggered by an all-time record set above the 3,000 level which caused a barrage of sell stop orders from the futures market, dealers said.

A lower Wall Street also spoiled the morning's record party. Profit taking remained limited until late in the afternoon. "There were big sell stop orders, in particular from (futures brokers) Fimat, in the 2,985-82 zone," a trader said.
The sales were made when the future, on the way back from the new record, fell through the zone.
The CAC-40 index closed down 29.42, or 0.98 percent, at 2,958.59. It set a all-time high at 3,006.54. The CAC-40 July futures ended at 2,966 versus 2,999 at Wednesday's close.
The broader SBF-120 index was down 18.22 at 2,021.14
Volume was 10.7 billion francs of which 8.1 billion in blue-chip shares.
Eurotunnel, up 4.55 percent at 6.90 francs, was the biggest gainer after recent sharp falls in the wake of a key debt deal and with some fears related to a strike call by French unions.
SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV was among the biggest fallers after it reported a 48 percent drop in first half profits.
